decisions.reason: As a core-adjacent upholstery fabric with its own product page, A likely meets at least modest aspiration levels and an established medium-sized textile firm in a growing market has enough slack to keep it while demand becomes clearer.

B is close to the firm's decorative range, but its weaker website prominence suggests more uncertain early acceptance, so management would probably keep it for now while monitoring whether results rise above aspiration.
C combines fit with the firm's curtain business and a functional flame-retardant feature valued in hospitality and project markets, so it is likely to perform above aspiration and be retained.

D builds on existing design and material capabilities, and although only mentioned rather than strongly featured, its adjacency and the firm's broad portfolio make retention more likely than withdrawal.

E appears the most niche and uncertain of the group and was only lightly signaled on the website, but given available slack and its closeness to the established collection, management would still be more likely to continue than to drop it immediately.
